newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insolvencies at postwar record in 96 - survey.
newsitem.headline: German insolvencies at postwar record in 96 - survey.

text.p: Germany last year suffered the highest number of corporate collapses in its postwar history, rising 15.5 percent to about 25,800, according to a survey by Dun & Bradstreet Schimmelpfeng released on Wednesday.
Insolvencies are set to hit a new record of about 28,000 in 1997 but the annual increase will slow to 10 percent, the business information company said in a statement.
In 1996, west Germany suffered about 18,000 company failures. In east Germany, some 7,700 companies collapsed, up 31 percent from 1995.

The construction sector was worst hit with about 7,100 firms collapsing. The retail and wholesale sectors, hit by persistently weak consumer spending, came second with 5,900 traders declaring insolvency and a total of 3,700 manufacturing businesses failed, Dun & Bradstreet said.
Outstanding payments are increasingly cited as a reason for company failures, alongside structural problems and management errors, Dun & Bradstreet said.
Official statistics for company insolvencies are available up to the end of September 1996. Dun & Bradstreet said it based its estimate for the full year on its own observations.
